attempts.label: DANDI:001960
attempts.paper_title: Large-scale all-optical electrophysiology links excitability and connectivity to circuit dynamics in vivo
attempts.entry_title: All-optical electrophysiology of layer 1 interneurons (Qi et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings hold up in this data: the intrinsic excitability groups, the synaptic and gap-junction connection counts (802 of 7,280 pairs in one mouse, exactly as published), the subthreshold dynamics, the link from excitability to spontaneous firing, and the NPY subtype differences. The synaptic length constant came out much longer than published, and the spikes lost or gained through connections did not match. Traveling waves and the interaction kernel did not reproduce, where the paper gives few method details. A small NPY gap-junction subtype effect appeared where the paper reports none, and single-spike SNR was lower than published. The Figure 1 tool-development claims could not be tested because those recordings are not in the dataset.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Qi, Parot, Wang, Pomeroy, Lavis and Cohen (2026) on dandiset 001960, which holds, for two NDNF-Cre::NPY-GFP mice, a spontaneous session, an intrinsic-excitability session and a connectivity-mapping session of about 320 layer 1 interneurons imaged at 787 Hz. It tests the intrinsic properties and their clusters, the synaptic and gap-junction connection maps and their structure, the spontaneous voltage and spike correlations, how excitability and connections shape spontaneous firing, and the differences between NPY-positive and NPY-negative cells. The tool-development experiments of Figure 1 and Supplementary Figures 1, 6, 9 and 18 are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Single-spike SNR (spike height over baseline shot noise) was 4.5 +/- 0.7; the estimated false-discovery proportion of spike detection was 17 +/- 13% and the false-negative rate 28 +/- 19%.
outcomes.source: Results, Molecular and optical tools, paragraph 5; Supplementary Figure 7
outcomes.quote: The single-spike SNR (spike-height:baseline shot noise) was 4.5 ± 0.7 (mean ± s.d.). Using a fitted mixture model, we estimated the spike-detection false-discovery proportion to be 17 ± 13% across all neurons, and false-negative rate to be 28 ± 19%
outcomes.notes: The stored voltage is normalized by each cell's spike height, so the SNR is 1 over the shot noise (1.4826 x MAD of the 1-frame difference). It is 3.33 over the 505 QC cells of the behavior sessions (3.18 over all 640) and 3.0 to 3.9 per mouse and session under every reading, below 4.5 +/- 0.7. With the spike heights found in the traces (median 0.88 to 0.96 SH) it is 2.8 to 3.0. The false-discovery and false-negative rates were not computed, since no matched-filter output or fitted mixture is stored, in the session files or in the raw-movie excerpt (its datasets are listed in the notebook); the SNR alone decides the outcome under every reading.
deviations: SNR from the stored normalized voltage, not from the raw fluorescence; the noise is the median over 3 min chunks (behavior sessions) or over 25 s samples of every fourth chunk (other sessions).
The error rates of the mixture model were not tested.

outcomes.statement: After 1 h of continuous imaging at 16 mW/mm2, spike SNR fell to 76 +/- 13% of its initial value.
outcomes.source: Results, Molecular and optical tools, paragraph 5; Supplementary Figure 8
outcomes.quote: After 1 h of continuous voltage imaging at 16 mW/mm 2 , the spike SNR decreased to 76 ± 13% of its initial value

Which session and which 520 cells the paper used is not given; the behavior sessions are the only sessions of an hour of continuous imaging, and QC cells and all cells are both shown.

outcomes.statement: During Hadamard-coded stimulation, stimulated cells fired at 25.4 +/- 16.6 Hz and non-stimulated cells at 3.9 +/- 4.5 Hz; each cell received about 640 stimuli and fired about 12,380 evoked spikes in total.
outcomes.source: Results, Gap junction coupling, paragraph 1

outcomes.notes: Over the 576 QC cells in the 160 Hadamard trials, 26.5 +/- 16.6 Hz with blue on and 3.6 +/- 4.2 Hz with it off; 12,929 evoked spikes per cell; 650 stimuli per cell counted as 750 ms code steps with blue on (reading (b)), and 360 counted as on blocks (reading (a)), since consecutive on steps merge into one block.

Assumed is reading (b), one stimulus per 750 ms code step with blue on, since the Methods describe the stimulation as Hadamard-Walsh codes of 750 ms steps; reading (a), on blocks, gives 360. Asked of the authors (findings).

outcomes.statement: Correcting the IPSP matrix for spikes evoked in non-targeted cells by lasso regression changes little; the corrected and raw matrices correlate with R = 0.82 and fewer than 20% of significant IPSPs differ by more than 20%.
outcomes.source: Methods, Analysis for mapping synaptic connections, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 16C
outcomes.quote: The two matrices are highly correlated, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.82, p < 2E-308, n = 1755 pairs from 2 mice, and less than 20% of statistically significant IPSPs differ from the connectivity matrix by more than 20%
outcomes.notes: Rebuilt from the 14,400 pulses of each sparsePulseHad session (each cell targeted 243 to 480 times, the paper's range). The rebuilt raw matrix matches the stored amplitudes only in part, R = 0.642 over the 1,753 of the 1,755 stored synaptic flags (955 + 800, the paper's n) that have an amplitude and 0.807 over those 60 to 400 um, with median -0.0183 against -0.0297 SH per spike. Under reading (a) the corrected matrix correlates with the raw at R = 0.937 (0.912 for 60 to 400 um), above 0.82 +/- 0.082, and 71.9% of the pairs differ by more than 20% (18.9% set to zero), not under 22%. Against the stored connectivity matrix, which is the paper's comparison, reading (a) gives R = 0.609 (0.779 for 60 to 400 um) and 91.1% of pairs differing by more than 20% (73.9% after scaling by the median ratio of stored to rebuilt raw, 1.31). Under reading (b) 99.9% of coefficients are zero (R = 0.054 with the raw, 0.049 with the stored). Least squares without a penalty still moves 37.0% of pairs by more than 20% of the raw (R = 0.970). The fraction is above 22% under every reading and both comparisons. Since the rebuilt raw matrix differs from the stored one, the failure may come from the reconstruction.
deviations: The per-pulse response is the mean normalized voltage 20 to 60 ms after pulse onset minus the 25 ms before (assumed; the paper gives no per-trial measure, and its fitted IPSP model is not run per pulse).

Spikes of a targeted cell are its stored estimated_spikes_per_blue_pulse (Methods); spikes of a non-targeted cell are its detected evoked spikes when it lies within 100 um of a target and zero elsewhere (assumed, from the 25 um off-target firing length constant of the Results).

The lasso is fitted per postsynaptic cell over pulses not targeting it, with an intercept for the blue-flash response, with scikit-learn's LassoCV (10 folds, 40 penalties, unstandardized predictors); the paper's software and settings are not given.
The 1755 pairs are taken to be the stored synaptic flags of both mice (955 and 800), which number 1755; the claims file says their choice is not given (asked of a reader in questions/001960.yaml).
Measured values are the corrected matrix against the rebuilt raw matrix under reading (a), the reconstruction's own before and after; the comparison with the stored matrix is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Synaptic connectivity had an exponential degree distribution, a connection probability of 24% for cells under 150 um apart and a length constant of about 105 um; gap junction probability was 83% under 150 um with a 159 um length constant.
outcomes.source: Results, The structure of connectivity in L1, paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 19C to F
outcomes.quote: The synaptic connectivity matrix had a single-scale network structure 47 , with an exponential degree distribution. The probability of connection was 24% for closely separated cells (< 150 μm) and fell with a ∼105 μm length constant (Supplementary Fig. 19C,D). The gap junction matrix showed greater connectivity (connection probability 83% for cells separated by < 150 μm) and fell with a 159 μm length constant
outcomes.notes: Synaptic probability under 150 um 23.5% and gap-junction 83.0%, both within tolerance. The gap-junction length constant is 156 um (log-linear, 30 um bins) or 161 um (60 um bins), within 159 +/- 15.9; least squares gives 184 um. The synaptic length constant is 176 to 180 um (log-linear) or 285 to 288 um (least squares), against 105 +/- 10.5 um, under every reading and in each mouse (151 to 362 um); the synaptic probability rises from 17% under 30 um to 29% at 90 to 120 um before it falls. The exponential degree fit is better for 3 of 4 degree distributions. Measured values are reading (b) with 30 um bins.

outcomes.statement: The population-average effect of one L1 spike is a brief excitatory pulse of about 2 ms spreading at 0.28 m/s with a decay length of about 160 um, followed by inhibition that peaks around 30 ms and decays with a time constant of about 35 ms.
outcomes.source: Results, The structure of connectivity in L1, paragraph 3; Supplementary Movie 3
outcomes.quote: a single L1 action potential evoked a brief excitatory pulse with a duration of ∼2 ms that rapidly propagated outward (0.28 m/s) with a ∼160 μm decay length constant, followed by a slower field of inhibition that peaked around 30 ms and decayed with a time constant of ∼35 ms
outcomes.notes: The population IPSP minimum is 33.0 ms after pulse onset (13 ms after its end), within 30 +/- 3 ms under reading (a); the decay after the peak is 39.4 ms with an offset and 47.9 ms without, against 35 +/- 3.5. findings.statement: Unit ids are per session and nothing links the cells of a mouse's three sessions. Cells with the same id lie a median 1.1 to 1.3 mm apart, and only 6 to 26 of 320 cells have a cell of the other session within 10 um, so either the sessions image different cells or their coordinates are in different frames; the files do not say which. The gfp_positive flags of a mouse also differ between sessions (156, 171 and 171 NPY+ cells in M-YQ0201-27; 135, 144 and 157 in M-YQ0201-29), so the paper's per-mouse counts (166 and 145 of 320) cannot be traced to a session.

The tool-development experiments of Figure 1 and Supplementary Figures 1, 5, 6, 9 and 18 (JF585 against JF608, wide-field against targeted images, the 76-cell stimulation, the lattice off-target test, the spinning-disk z-stack, the 7.5x recordings) are not in the dandiset, and the raw-movie excerpt holds only projections of the structural stacks.

The paper's connection and pair counts (802 of 7,280, 667 of 7,032, 3,553 and 2,199) are those of ordered pairs of passed_qc cells 60 to 400 um apart, and the passed_qc flag differs by session (the code documents its two rules); neither the band nor the rules are stated in the files.

ipsp_decay_source_units and its standard error carry no unit (the file says so); the values are consistent with seconds (median 0.035, capped at 0.4). membrane_time_constant_ms is exactly 0 for 7 cells of M-YQ0201-27, with no flag marking a failed fit. The x and y origin is undocumented. The x and y axes are not oriented on the brain (no anterior, posterior, medial or lateral direction is stored), so the directions of the wave analysis can be given only in the image frame.

The code's Figure 3 loader says the pairwise table's presynaptic and postsynaptic id columns vary in the opposite order to its metric columns. In this version they agree (row k is presynaptic k mod 320, postsynaptic k // 320), as the stored presynaptic spike times per row confirm.

For the authors. Single-spike SNR; how is the spike height entering the SNR of 4.5 measured? The stored normalized voltage gives 3.3 (1 over 1.4826 x MAD of the 1-frame difference), and 3.0 to 3.9 per session.

For the authors. Supplementary Movie 3 (interaction-kernel); how were the 2 ms pulse duration, the 30 ms peak, the 35 ms decay and the 160 um length constant measured? The population spikelet waveform has a 22.7 ms FWHM and probability times amplitude falls with 72 to 96 um.

For the authors. Spikes lost and gained (Figure 5E, 5G); over which window is the rate integrated ("the entire IPSP duration", "the entire spikelet duration"), and against which baseline? Readings give 2.9e-3 to 1.6e-2 spikes lost for the top quintile and ratios of the balance from -0.19 to 6.96.

For the authors. Wave propagation analysis; how were peaks of the derivative separated or merged, was the derivative smoothed, in what window were the flanking minimum and maximum sought, and is lag signed or absolute against separation? Spans between adjacent turning points give 4,446 events and 10.1 mm/s, spans within 250 ms 3,775 events and 6.2 mm/s; lag regressed on distance gives hundreds of mm/s.
For the authors. Hadamard stimulation; are the "640 stimuli" per cell the 750 ms code steps with blue on? Counting steps gives 650, counting contiguous on blocks gives 360.

For the authors. P(spk|V) (Figure 4E, F); is V the sample at the spike frame (as the code computes and the Methods' V(t_s) says) or the voltage in the 10 ms before the spike (the Results and the Figure 4E legend)? With the spike frame 52% of cells have a sigmoid fit with R^2 >= 0.9, with the mean of the 10 ms before 42%, with the sample 10 ms before 24%.

For the authors. Supplementary Figure 26A; is a cell's spike rate and voltage at oscillation peaks the value at the peak or a mean over a window? At the peak the voltages do not differ (p = 0.22), over +/-300 frames they do (p = 0.022).

For the authors. Detection limits and the lasso correction; which 100 pairs near the cutoff, how the 50% point was estimated, which per-trial response entered the lasso, and its penalty. The per-pair statistics and nulls are not stored. A rebuilt lasso (per-pulse voltage 20 to 60 ms after onset, cross-validated penalty) gives R = 0.94 with the raw matrix and 72% of pairs changed by more than 20%.
For the authors. IPSP durations (Supplementary Fig. 25C); were decay fits that end on the 0.4 s bound left out? Left out, the means are 57.1 and 41.9 ms (paper 58 and 43); kept, 77.4 and 65.2 ms.

entries.title: All-optical electrophysiology of layer 1 interneurons (Qi et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Qi, Parot, Wang, Pomeroy, Lavis and Cohen (2026) on dandiset 001960, which holds, for two NDNF-Cre::NPY-GFP mice, a spontaneous session, an intrinsic-excitability session and a connectivity-mapping session of about 320 layer 1 interneurons imaged at 787 Hz. It tests the intrinsic properties and their clusters, the synaptic and gap-junction connection maps and their structure, the spontaneous voltage and spike correlations, how excitability and connections shape spontaneous firing, and the differences between NPY-positive and NPY-negative cells. The tool-development experiments of Figure 1 and Supplementary Figures 1, 6, 9 and 18 are not in the dandiset.
